;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Sehwan suicide bombing|2017 Sehwan suicide bombing]]
**At least 70 people are killed and more than 150 injured in [[suicide bombing]] at [[Shrine of Lal Shahbaz Qalandar|Lal Shahbaz Qalandar Shrine]] in [[Sehwan]], [[Sindh]], [[Pakistan]]; 50 of the injured are in critical condition, medical emergency has been declared in the hospitals of [[Hyderabad, Pakistan|Hyderabad]], [[Dadu District|Dadu]] and [[Jamshoro]]. [http://www.dawn.com/news/1315136/at-least-10-dead-as-bomb-rips-through-lal-shahbaz-shrine-in-sehwan-sindh (Dawn News)] [https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/186748-Several-injured-in-Sehwan-Sharif-explosion# (The News)]
*[[Iraqi Civil War (2014–2017)]]
**A car bomb explodes in a [[Shia Islam|Shi'ite]] neighbourhood in [[Baghdad]], killing at least 48 people. [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] claimed responsibility for the bombing. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-38995832 (BBC)]
*[[Rohingya genocide|2016–17 Rohingya persecution in Myanmar]]
**According to [[Tatmadaw|Myanmar's military]], it has ended its "clearance operation" against the country's [[Rohingya people|Rohingya minority]] in [[Rakhine State]], which the [[United Nations]] says may amount to [[ethnic cleansing]] and [[crimes against humanity]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/feb/16/myanmar-military-crackdown-against-rohingyas-has-ceased (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)]]
**An air raid on a funeral in a village north of [[Sana'a]] kills at least eight women and children. The [[Houthis]] blames the [[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen|Saudi-led coalition]] for the attack. [http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/02/air-raid-yemen-funeral-kills-women-170216093707979.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*[[2014–17 Venezuelan protests|Venezuelan protests]]
**[[Venezuela]]'s [[Supreme Tribunal of Justice (Venezuela)|Supreme Tribunal of Justice]] upholds the 13-year, 9-month-plus prison term of [[Popular Will]] party founder [[Leopoldo  López]]  for  inciting  violence, via "subliminal messages,"  at  the   2014 anti-government protests where 43 people were killed.  Yesterday, [[President of the United States|United States President]] [[Donald Trump]]  met with López's wife, [[Lilian Tintori]], and called on Venezuela to release López immediately.   [http://laht.com/article.asp?CategoryId=10717&ArticleId=2431305 (''Latin American Herald Tribune'')] [http://mobile.reuters.com/article/idUSKBN15V01F (Reuters)] [http://heavy.com/news/2017/02/leopoldo-lopez-donald-trump-venezuela-who-is-bio-wife-lilian-tintori-twitter-release-political-prisoner-marco-rubio/ (Heavy.com)]
*[[Legal challenges to Executive Order 13769|Legal challenges to U.S. immigration suspension order]]
**The [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Justice Department]] tells the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit|Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals]] that it won't be seeking further action by the court since this executive order will soon be replaced by a different one.  Justice added they expect the Ninth Circuit ruling will be vacated once the new executive order is issued. [http://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/justice-department-opposes-new-hearing-trump-travel-restrictions-n722011?google_editors_picks=true (NBC News)]
;Politics and elections
*[[First presidency of Donald Trump|Presidency of Donald Trump]]
**[[Protests against Donald Trump]]
***[[Executive Order 13769|U.S. immigration suspension]], [[Day Without Immigrants (2017)|Day Without Immigrants]]
****Hundreds of restaurants and other businesses in U.S. cities close their doors after activists called on immigrants to stay home from work, avoid shopping or eating out, and skip classes Thursday for #ADayWithoutImmigrants, to protest [[President of the United States|the President]]'s [[Immigration policy of the first Donald Trump administration|immigration reforms]] and highlight the immigrant community's contributions to the [[United States]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usta-immigration-protest-idUSKBN15V19M (Reuters)] [https://www.theatlantic.com/business/archive/2017/02/day-without-immigrants/516969/ (''The Atlantic'')] [http://www.philly.com/philly/news/pennsylvania/A-Day-Without-Immigrtants-Redux.html (''The Philadelphia Inquirer'')] [http://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-ln-lausd-phone-message-20170215-story.html (''Los Angeles Times'')]
**[[First cabinet of Donald Trump|Formation of Donald Trump's cabinet]]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] names  [[Florida International University College of Law]] Dean  and former [[National Labor Relations Board]] member [[Alexander Acosta]] to be [[United States Secretary of Labor|Secretary of Labor]]. The President's initial nominee, [[Andy Puzder]], withdrew his nomination yesterday. [http://www.politico.com/story/2017/02/trump-to-announce-alexander-acosta-as-labor-secretary-nominee-235089 (Politico)] [http://www.cnn.com/2017/02/16/politics/donald-trump-white-house-announcement/ (CNN)] [https://www.npr.org/2017/02/16/515585143/watch-trump-to-announce-new-labor-nominee (NPR)]
**[[Political appointments of the first Trump administration|Political appointments of Donald Trump]]
***The [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] confirms, 51-49, Congressman [[Mick Mulvaney]] to head the [[Office of Management and Budget]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/wonk/wp/2017/02/16/senators-confirm-trumps-pick-to-deal-with-the-federal-budget/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2016 Philippine presidential election|Philippine presidential election, 2016]]
**The [[Supreme Court of the Philippines|Supreme Court]] of the [[Philippines]] allows the electoral protest of defeated candidate  [[Bongbong Marcos]] against [[Vice President of the Philippines|Philippine vice president]]  [[Leni Robredo]] to continue. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2017-02-16/philippine-supreme-court-allows-election-recount-for-defeated-marcos (Reuters via ''U.S. News and World Report'')]
*[[United Nations]] officials announce the creation of a new team in [[Geneva]] to investigate possible [[war crimes]], [[crimes against humanity]] and [[genocide]] during the [[Syrian Civil War]] in order to prepare for future prosecutions of those responsible. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/feb/16/syria-un-sets-up-unit-to-aid-prosecutions-of-war-crimes (''The Guardian'')]
